_comment: REFERENCE FILE — shows every field, type and format JLPT Practice understands. Do not load this file as a test; copy the shape you need. Required keys per question: id, type, question, and either options+answer (multiple choice) or format:"typed"+correctAnswers. All other keys are optional.
title: Example — Every Question Type and Format
description: A annotated example set: 5 categories × multiple-choice and typed formats, with every optional field demonstrated. Question type is kanji | vocabulary | grammar | reading | expression.

questions.question: 「日」の意味は何ですか？
questions.explanation: 日 (nichi/hi) = day or sun. Appears in 日本 (Japan) and 毎日 (every day).

questions.question: Translate 学校 into English.
questions.explanation: 学校 (がっこう, gakkō) means school.

questions.question: わたし ___ 学生です。
questions.explanation: は marks the topic of the sentence: “As for me, (I) am a student.”

questions.question: きのう、ともだちと こうえん へ 行きました。What did the writer do yesterday?
options: Went to the park with a friend
questions.explanation: 行きました (went) + こうえん (park) + ともだちと (with a friend).

questions.question: How do you say “Good morning” in Japanese? (romaji is fine)
questions.explanation: おはようございます (ohayō gozaimasu) is the polite morning greeting.

questions.question: What is the on'yomi reading of 山? Type only the romaji.
questions.explanation: 山 has two readings: さん (san, on'yomi — as in 富士山) and やま (yama, kun'yomi). Strict mode = no typo tolerance.

questions.question: Which kanji means “person”?
questions.explanation: 人 (hito) = person; じん is the on'yomi, as in 日本人.

questions.question: A shopkeeper says いらっしゃいませ. What are they doing? Answer in English.
questions.hint: Think about what staff say when you enter
questions.explanation: いらっしゃいませ is the standard welcome to a customer entering a shop or restaurant.
